newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Copper climbs on strike, wheat and oil down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Copper climbs on strike, wheat and oil down.

text.p: Wheat markets eased on Wednesday as forecasts for improving weather weighed on prices that had risen sharply recently on floods and a freeze in North America and a dry spell in Europe.
Copper prices rose as a strike in Chile's Escondida mine boosted the market.
Other commodity markets saw coffee futures pull back some of Tuesday's losses on the back of a strong U.S. market. Cocoa futures were seen buoyed by trade buying and supply concerns.

Wheat prices were slightly softer on Wednesday. Chicago Board of Trade soft red winter wheat futures for May were pressured lower at the midsession, trading at around $4.38 a bushel, down some three cents.
Forecasts for rain in France and scepticism over a report on Tuesday which pegged recent freeze losses in the U.S. Great Plains at up to 290 million bushels helped drag the market lower.
"There's a forecast for rain in France Friday, Sunday and Monday and that's taking us down," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
A prolonged dry spell in much of Europe had boosted wheat prices for most of last week, with floods and freezing weather condition in some areas of the United States,

But weather conditions are still a worry, and the decline was limited by flooding in the northern U.S. spring wheat growing region which continues to slow spring wheat seedings and concerns over dry weather in portions of Australia and Europe.

London Metal Exchange copper was boosted on Tuesday by news of a strike at the Escondida mine, the world's largest copper mine, in Chile. On Wednesday the market was digesting news that union leaders at the mine had recommended acceptance of a pay deal, to be voted on today.
Voting should be finished by 1700 local time (2100 GMT) and the result known almost immediately, Pablo Godoy, of the Chilean Mining Confederation, which is advising the Escondida union, told Reuters.
Nearby tightness in the market also helped to push prices higher. Copper was trading at $2,382 a tonne as the vote result was awaited.
Aluminium cemented gains above the $1,600 level after stocks recorded another hefty fall of 5,225 tonnes on Wednesday.
Coffee futures clawed back the day's losses to finish slightly higher in London, helped up by strength in New York.
Coffee futures of the arabica type in New York rocketed higher in early morning trade after talks to end a truckers' strike in Colombia, the world's second largest coffee producer, collapsed.
London robusta coffee futures did not recover as strongly, but managed to rise above the day's low of $1,610 a tonne.

Robusta coffee futures reached to $1,632 a tonne in London's afternoon. Arabicas were still firm but off the day's highs, with July futures at 192 cents per pound, up 3.65 cents on the day but off an earlier peak of 196.

Stronger cocoa futures were largely lifted higher by trade buying in London. Fundamentally traders said prices were still being buoyed by talk some Ivory Coast shippers were having difficulty fulfilling commitments despite large Ivorian arrivals. Some traders said bean quality could be hampering supply.

World oil prices had a stronger morning in London on mildly bullish American Petroleum Institute stocks data, but later came under pressure from sluggish gas oil and poor demand for other oil products, such as gasoline and heavy fuel, in Europe.
Benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude oil futures for July hovered around the $18 a barrel level in London's afternoon, slipping below it in London's late afternoon.
Meanwhile gold took a knock after an analyst suggested that central banks could activate reserves, but it pared its losses to remain trapped in its range of $340 to $345 of the last week.
Some key prices at 1730 GMT on Wednesday.
